accountsTotal.description: §3.13: how many accounts are in the room, whether or not this answer served them.

accountsServed.description: §3.13: how many rows this answer carries. Below the total when the cap fired; --full lifts it.

kamiCount.description: Compact form: how many kamis the account has here. The roster itself is `--full` or the party/roster queries.

RoomExit.description: §3.13 (0.5.0): one way out of a room. getExitsFor has been in the ported tree since 0.1.0 and no query ever called it, so no served surface anywhere named a room connection and a reader could learn the map only by moving and failing — which §3.11 exists to refuse. Served verbatim as the pinned client computes it: special exits (the room's Exits component) followed by geometric neighbours, NOT de-duplicated and NOT symmetrised, because the client renders exactly this list.

gates.description: Conditions on entering the destination; empty for an ungated exit. FACTS ONLY — whether a given account passes them is the reader's own evaluation.

Condition.description: One condition the world stores on an exit, with the pinned client's own words for it beside the raw target. FACTS ONLY: whether a given account passes it is the reader's own evaluation — this surface takes no account argument, and inventing a per-viewer verdict would be mirroring a pane rather than serving the state (§3.11). Its `value` is a string for the reason given on that field.

value.description: VERBATIM, as a string (§1.2). A condition's value is not always a count — a room gate's is an entity id, and Number() on an id-sized uint returns 2.65e+76: a value the world does not hold and nothing can join on.

text.description: parseConditionalText, verbatim including the pin's spacing quirks.
